price: 225; 275; 325.

Problem 2:

5. The squad that won 3 gold medals, the squad that won 6 silver medals and the squad from Bolivia were all different teams.
6. Neither the team from Argentina nor the squad that won 2 silver medals is the squad that won 4 gold medals.
8. The squad that won 2 gold medals is either the squad that won 6 silver medals or the team from Grenada.

% We assign a country C with silver medals S and gold medals G, where C belongs to country, S belongs to silver_medals, and G belongs to gold_medals.

{C1=C2; S1=S2; G1=G2}=0 :- assign(C1,S1,G1), assign(C2,S2,G2), (C1,S1,G1)!=(C2,S2,G2).

C1!=C3 :- assign(C1,S1,G1), assign(C2,S2,G2), assign(C3,S3,G3), G1=3, S2=6, C3="Bolivia".

% 1.1 The bird bought in February and the bird bought in January are different.
M1!=M2 :- owns(N1,M1,B1), owns(N2,M2,B2), M1=2, M2=1.

% 1.2 The bird bought in February is Gladys's or the macaw.
{N="Gladys"; B="macaw"}=1 :- owns(N,M,B), M=2.

% 1.3 The bird bought in January is Gladys's or the macaw.
{N="Gladys"; B="macaw"}=1 :- owns(N,M,B), M=1.

% 2. The macaw was bought 2 months before Ellen's pet.
M1=M2-2 :- owns(N1,M1,B1), owns(N2,M2,B2), B1="macaw", N2="Ellen".

% 3. The parakeet was bought 1 month after the finch.
M1=M2+1 :- owns(N1,M1,B1), owns(N2,M2,B2), B1="parakeet", B2="finch".

% 4. Alberta's pet was bought 1 month before Gladys's pet.
M1=M2-1 :- owns(N1,M1,B1), owns(N2,M2,B2), N1="Alberta", N2="Gladys".

% 5. The finch was bought sometime after the lovebird.
M1>M2 :- owns(N1,M1,B1), owns(N2,M2,B2), B1="finch", B2="lovebird".
